newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI Apr 96-Feb 97 support to India govt Rs 120 bln.
newsitem.headline: RBI Apr 96-Feb 97 support to India govt Rs 120 bln.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India's direct support to the government in primary issues of dated securities and treasury bills was around 120 billion rupees during April 1996 and February 1997, central bank chief Chakravarty Rangarajan said on Wednesday.
The net RBI credit to the government during this period was only 50 billion rupees due to the fact that the central bank undertook active open-market operations, he said in a statement.
The repos operations by RBI similarly resulted in sales of about 15 billion rupees at the end of this period, he said.
Rangarajan said there were misconceptions that the new system of ways and means advances, announced on Wednesday, was simply a variant of the earlier ad hoc treasury bills, which it seeks to replace.
"A question often raised is whether the new scheme of ways and means advances is not old wine in new bottle," he said.
Earlier on Wednesday, the RBI and the Indian government signed an agreement to abolish the issue of ad hoc treasury bills from April 1, 1997 and replace it with a system of ways and means advances.
"While ad hocs were used to monetise budget deficits year after year in a cumulative way, ways and means advances is not a source of financing deficit at all," Rangarajan said.
He said the new system will purely be a mechanism for bridging the gap between the government's expenditure and revenue temporarily and will be vacated from time to time.
Rangarajan said the monetised deficit figure of 160 billion rupeees shown in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget announced in February should be taken as purely indicative.
"The actual level could turn out to be different due to the Reserve Bank's operations in the market," he said.
